done_when: The guard allows rm -rf when every target, resolved, is inside the system temp folder (TMPDIR, /tmp or /private/tmp), and allows reading git config values (git config --get, or git config with a key and no value); everything it blocks today otherwise stays blocked.

findings.body: With a hook payload cwd inside temp, `cd /etc && rm -rf config` is allowed. The guard passes the original cwd to every parsed command, so it resolves `config` inside temp even though the shell runs `rm` from `/etc`. This violates the requirement that every target resolve inside temp. Track directory changes or keep such relative targets blocked.
findings.title: Not done: Resolve rm targets from the shell's directory at execution

findings.body: With the hook process's `TMPDIR` inside temp, `TMPDIR=/etc; rm -rf "$TMPDIR/config"` passes: `os.path.expandvars` uses the hook's original environment, while the shell uses its newly assigned value and targets `/etc/config`. This is distinct from the ruling on leftover `$VAR`: the token leaves no `$` after expansion, but the expansion is stale. A single-quoted `$TMPDIR` is also expanded here even though the shell leaves it literal.
findings.title: Block rm targets whose variable value changes before execution

findings.body: The end-to-end blocked cases exercise fixed payload directories and inherited variables. Add `forge hook deny` cases for `cd` before a relative `rm -rf` and for reassignment of `TMPDIR` before removal. The current test passes while both commands above bypass the guard.
findings.title: Not done: Test rejection after shell directory and variable changes

why: The destructive-command guard blocks rm -rf even inside the system temp folder where coordinators keep scratch clones, and blocks reading a git config value, so scratch clones pile up and coordinators work around the guard
